Each bar is how long the line was busy that day out of 12 hours — filling plus the minutes lost to an oil change. Colour is the oil that filled the most litres on that line that day; a very short run still gets a sliver so you can see it happened. Hatched columns are Sundays, a grey baseline means the line stood idle on a working day. The bottom row is all six lines together, as a percentage of the 72 line-hours a day gives you.

Why the bars are flat until day 3

Day 3
Mon 3 Aug — the first day the floor was full

For the first 1 working days of August the lines barely moved. The best of them, Sat 1 Aug, used 0% of the day; every one of those days carries the same one-line reason in the replay — godown full, production capped to what can ship. On Sat 1 Aug the finished-goods godown stood at 112.3% of its 8,27,000 L ceiling, with -1,01,314 L of room — about -101 thousand litres to play with when a single full day makes 1,24,307 L. There was nowhere to put the oil, so the machines waited.

Then the trucks came. Sat 1 Aug alone moved 256 L out, and by the morning of Mon 3 Aug the godown had fallen to 82.1% — 1,48,050 L free, -1× the room it had the working day before. That day carries no cap at all: all six lines ran the full 12 hours, 72 of 72 line-hours, 10 runs, 1,24,307 L, ₹2.38 Cr. It happened 10 times all month. The cap was back on Fri 7 Aug and covered 11 of the 24 working days that were left.

So the flat bars are not a machine problem. Every one of the 799 blocked SKU-days in the month is held by a material — packaging or oil. None is held by a line. The floor gave back 35% of its hours while the godown sat at its ceiling.

Measured, and assumed

Line speeds are measured. The hours on this page are not: the replay fills at the rated speed, and says so — “rated line speed, not the NaN% observed”. At the observed rate every bar above would be longer.

A dash means that bottle size is not set up on that line. Sizes are the only thing that ties a product to a machine — any oil runs on any line.

This is a replay, not a record. It shows what the planner would have done in August 2026, standing on each morning with no later data. The factory did not run this way.
Measured: the order book, opening stock, BOMs, line speeds, realise (May–Jul), lead times, storage ceiling, and the people. Assumed: supply arrives exactly on lead time; a 2-day invoice→truck lag; rated line speed rather than the 47% observed. WhatsApp replies are written in by the simulation, not received.
Every number traces to sim/sim-inputs.json.
